ideas_today.title: Real-Time Sensor Data Aggregator with C and JavaScript
ideas_today.why: This project demonstrates the ability to bridge low-level system performance with high-level web interfaces, a common requirement in IoT and real-time analytics platforms. Measured demand - C: in 11% of 84 postings over 30 days (+16.6 pp vs previous 7 days); trend score 0.08. JavaScript: in 29% of 84 postings over 30 days (-20.8 pp vs previous 7 days); trend score 0.38.
ideas_today.scope: Build a lightweight C daemon that reads simulated sensor data from stdin or a file, aggregates it using a ring buffer, and exposes a JSON endpoint via a minimal HTTP server. Create a simple JavaScript frontend that polls this endpoint to visualize live temperature trends on a canvas.
success_metrics: C daemon processes 10,000 sensor readings per second without memory leaks
JavaScript dashboard updates visualization within 200ms of new data arrival
Unit tests cover all core aggregation logic in C

ideas_today.title: Distributed Task Queue with Agile Workflow Integration
ideas_today.why: It showcases proficiency in building scalable backend infrastructure while adhering to modern software development methodologies like Agile, which is critical for team-based engineering roles. Measured demand - Distributed Systems: in 10% of 84 postings over 30 days (-1.7 pp vs previous 7 days); trend score 0.00. Agile: in 8% of 84 postings over 30 days (-1.7 pp vs previous 7 days); trend score 0.00.
ideas_today.scope: Implement a basic distributed task queue in Python where workers pull jobs from a Redis list. Integrate this with a Jira-like API mock to demonstrate Agile workflow tracking (e.g., moving tickets from 'In Progress' to 'Done' upon job completion). Document the sprint planning process used to build this feature.
success_metrics: System successfully distributes tasks across 3 concurrent worker processes
Task status updates are reflected in the mock Agile board within 1 second
Integration tests verify end-to-end task lifecycle from submission to completion

ideas_today.title: Statistical Outlier Detection Library in R
ideas_today.why: This highlights specialized statistical analysis capabilities often required in data science teams, complementing general programming skills with domain-specific expertise. Measured demand - Data Analysis: in 15% of 84 postings over 30 days (+3.6 pp vs previous 7 days); trend score 0.04. R: in 8% of 84 postings over 30 days (+0.8 pp vs previous 7 days); trend score 0.04.
ideas_today.scope: Develop an R package that implements multiple outlier detection algorithms (Z-score, IQR, Mahalanobis distance) for tabular data. Include a CLI interface to run these analyses on CSV files and generate summary reports. Write comprehensive unit tests for each algorithm.
success_metrics: Package passes all unit tests for edge cases (empty datasets, single values)
Execution time for analyzing a 100k-row dataset is under 5 seconds
Documentation includes clear usage examples for each detection method
